title: Ten jurors, one vote each
rules: Ten jurors per country each gave one point to one song.
effect: With so few points, no vote can be far from the average.

title: Top three: 3, 2, 1
rules: Each jury gave 3, 2 and 1 points to its three favourites.
effect: The fewest points of any year, and the lowest curve.

title: Top five: 5 to 1
effect: More than twice the points of 1962, so the curve nearly doubles.

title: Top three: 5, 3, 1
rules: Ten jurors again, three songs worth 5, 3 and 1.
effect: Fewer points, and the curve drops back.

title: One vote per juror again
rules: The 1957 rules returned: ten jurors, one point each.

title: Every song scored
rules: Two jurors per country gave every song 1 to 5 points.
effect: Many more points, but every song got some, so scores stayed close and the curve rose only a little.

title: Ten points, one last time
rules: One year back on ten jurors with one vote each.
effect: The curve falls at once. Only the rules changed.

title: Douze points
rules: 12, 10, 8–1 to ten songs, nothing to the rest. Televoting (1998), semi-finals (2004) and juries returning (2009) all kept this one set of points.
effect: Ten songs score and the others get zero, so every vote lands far from the average. The curve jumps and then stays flat for 40 years.

title: Jury and televote apart
rules: Jury and viewers each give their own 12, 10, 8–1.
effect: Twice the points lifts the curve. On the same scale this is the lowest period of all.
